title: Aqeedah
sub: Learn about Allah, His Messengers ﷺ and the Last Day

lessons.title: Why we learn belief
lessons.about: Why every Muslim must know what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah.

cards.x: Aqeedah means belief: what a Muslim holds to be true in the heart. Every Muslim who has reached adulthood and is sane must know what is necessary for Allah, what is impossible for Him, and what is possible for Him, and the same for the Messengers عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Scholars sort everything the mind can think of into three. Necessary (wajib): the mind cannot picture it not being there, like Allah's existence. Impossible (mustahil): the mind cannot picture it existing, like Allah having a partner. Possible (ja'iz): it may exist or not, like rain tomorrow.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

cards.x: Knowing these things protects your belief from doubt. You don't need to be a scholar: you need to know them clearly and be sure of them.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, opening: the three judgements

checks.q: Knowing what is necessary, impossible and possible for Allah is a duty on whom?
checks.a: Every sane Muslim who has reached adulthood
w: Only people who were not born Muslim
checks.why: Umm al-Barahin makes it a duty on every sane adult Muslim, not only on scholars, because belief must rest on knowledge.

checks.q: In aqeedah, something the mind cannot picture not existing is called…
checks.why: Necessary means the mind cannot picture it absent. Allah's existence is the clearest example.

checks.q: In aqeedah, something that may exist or may not, like rain tomorrow, is called…
checks.why: Everything in creation is possible: it can be or not be, and only exists because Allah brings it into being.

checks.q: Allah having a partner is, for the mind…
checks.why: The mind cannot picture two gods each in full control, so a partner for Allah is impossible.

lessons.title: Islam, Iman and Ihsan
lessons.about: The famous hadith of Jibril: the three levels of the religion.

cards.x: Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ came in the form of a man and asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, Iman, Ihsan and the Hour, so the Companions could learn their religion. Muslim narrated it from 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: To bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, to establish the prayer, pay zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj if you are able.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: To worship Allah as though you see Him; and though you do not see Him, He sees you.
cards.src: Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

checks.q: In the hadith of Jibril, how many pillars of Islam are there?
checks.why: The two testimonies, prayer, zakat, fasting Ramadan and Hajj for those able.

checks.q: Which of these is one of the six articles of Iman, not a pillar of Islam?
checks.why: Islam is the outward pillars; Iman is what is believed in the heart.

checks.q: What is Ihsan?
checks.a: Worshipping Allah as though you see Him
checks.why: And though you do not see Him, He sees you. It is the highest level of the religion.

checks.q: Who came asking the Prophet ﷺ these questions?
checks.a: Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, in the form of a man
w: An angel no one could see
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ said afterwards: that was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion.

lessons.title: How we know Allah exists
lessons.about: Imam al-Sanusi's proof from the world around us.

cards.x: Look at the world: things move then stop, grow then fade, arrive then leave. Each new state had a beginning. Imam al-Sanusi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says something that is never free of changes that begin must itself have begun. So the world came into being; it has not always been there.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.x: Something that came into being cannot bring itself into being, just as a house does not build itself. So the world needs a Maker who did not come into being: Allah.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, proof of His existence

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi gives a proof for each attribute he mentions, so that the believer holds each one with understanding and not only by copying others (taqlid).
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the proofs of the attributes

checks.q: Imam al-Sanusi proves the world had a beginning. What does he point to?
w: Everything in it is very old
checks.why: Things move then stop, grow then fade. Each new state began, and something never free of beginnings must itself have begun.

checks.q: Once we know the world had a beginning, why does it need a Maker?
checks.a: Something that began cannot bring itself into being
w: Something so vast cannot be explained by chance
Something so ordered must have been designed by people
Something that began will one day end by itself
checks.why: A house does not build itself. What came into being needs someone to bring it into being: Allah.

checks.q: Could the Maker of the world also have had a beginning?
checks.a: No, otherwise He too would need a maker, without end
w: Yes, as long as it began before the world
Yes, if it began at the same moment as the world
We cannot know, so we leave it to the scholars
checks.why: If the Maker began, He would need a maker, and that one another, forever. So the Maker has no beginning.

checks.q: Why does al-Sanusi give a proof for each attribute of Allah?
checks.a: So the believer holds belief with understanding, not only by copying
w: So the believer can win every debate with others
So the believer can leave faith and rely on proofs
So the book matches the books of the philosophers
checks.why: He wants each Muslim to know why, so their belief is firm against doubt.

lessons.title: Allah exists, without beginning or end
lessons.about: Allah exists, with no beginning and no end, depending on nothing.

cards.x: Allah exists. His existence has no cause and does not depend on anything.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah has no beginning (qidam). Everything else came into being after not existing; He did not.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never cease to be. As Imam al-Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says: He is Eternal without a beginning and Everlasting without an end.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Allah's Oneness

checks.q: Allah has no beginning (qidam). What does that mean?
checks.a: He never came into being; He always was
w: He was created before everything else
He began when the universe began
checks.why: Qidam means Allah never came into being. Everything else existed after not existing; He did not.

checks.q: Allah has no end (baqa'). What does that mean?
checks.a: He will never cease to exist
w: He will end after the Last Day
He ends when the world ends
checks.why: Baqa' means He never ceases. Al-Tahawi: Eternal without a beginning, Everlasting without an end.

checks.q: Does Allah's existence depend on anything, the way ours depends on Him?
checks.why: Allah's existence has no cause. Everything else depends on Him.

checks.q: Why must Allah have no beginning?
checks.a: If He had a beginning, He would need a maker, like everything that begins
w: Because the world is very old, so He must be older
Because time began with Him, so He is its start
Because the angels testify that He came first
checks.why: Anything that begins needs a cause. Allah needs nothing, so He has no beginning.

lessons.title: Allah is unlike anything
lessons.about: Allah does not resemble His creation, needs nothing, and is One.

cards.x: Allah does not resemble anything He created. He is not a body, He is not in a place, and He is not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.' (al-Shura 11)
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah stands by Himself (qiyam bi-nafsihi): He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being. Everything needs Him.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

cards.x: Allah is One (wahdaniyyah): One in His Self, One in His attributes and One in His actions. He has no partner and no equal.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

checks.q: Which of these is true about Allah?
checks.a: He does not resemble anything He created
w: He has a body unlike ours
He is in one particular place
He is bound by time like us
checks.why: Allah is not a body, not in a place and not bound by time. 'There is nothing like Him.' (al-Shura 11)

checks.q: Allah 'stands by Himself' (qiyam bi-nafsihi). What does that mean?
checks.a: He needs nothing, while everything needs Him
w: He sits on His Throne, which holds Him up
He stands in one place above His creation
He needs our worship, while we need His mercy
checks.why: He needs no place and no one to bring Him into being, while all things need Him.

checks.q: Allah is One (wahdaniyyah). His Oneness covers…
checks.a: His Self, His attributes and His actions
w: His Self only, while His actions are shared
His Self and His attributes, but not His actions
His actions only, since His Self is unknown
checks.why: No one shares His Self, no one has attributes like His, and no one else truly creates.

checks.q: Which verse sums up that Allah is unlike creation?
checks.a: 'There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing'
w: 'Read in the name of your Lord'
'Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth'
'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak'
checks.why: Al-Shura 11 denies any likeness, and still affirms hearing and sight, without likeness.

lessons.title: Seven attributes of Allah
lessons.about: Power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.

cards.x: Allah has Power (qudrah) over every possible thing, and Will (iradah): nothing happens except what He wills.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Allah has Knowledge ('ilm) of everything: what was, what is, what will be, and what would be. He is Living (hayah) with a life unlike ours.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Allah hears (sam') and sees (basar) all that exists, without ears or eyes. He speaks (kalam) with an eternal speech that is not letters or sounds. The Qur'an is His speech.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: Umm al-Barahin lists twenty necessary attributes. Existence (wujud). Five that negate what does not befit Him (salbiyyah): no beginning, no end, unlike creation, needing nothing, and Oneness. Seven attributes of meaning (ma'ani): power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech. And seven that follow from those: that He is Powerful, Willing, Knowing, Living, Hearing, Seeing and Speaking.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the attributes of meaning

cards.x: The Maturidis, the school of Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ followed by most Hanafis, add an eighth attribute of meaning: takwin, Allah's bringing things into being. The Ash'aris count this under power and will. Both schools are Ahl al-Sunnah.
cards.src: al-'Aqa'id al-Nasafiyyah, the attributes

checks.q: Allah has the attribute of will (iradah). So in creation…
checks.a: Nothing happens except what He wills
checks.why: Nothing happens in His kingdom except what He wills, good or bad.

checks.q: Allah hears and sees. How?
checks.a: Without ears or eyes, unlike creation
w: With ears and eyes like ours
He does not hear or see
checks.why: His attributes are real but unlike ours. He hears every sound and sees everything without organs.

checks.q: Allah's attribute of speech (kalam) is…
checks.a: Eternal, and not made of letters or sounds
w: Created, and made of letters and sounds
Eternal, but made of Arabic letters and sounds
Began with the first revelation to the Prophets
checks.why: His speech has no beginning. The Qur'an is His speech.

checks.q: How many necessary attributes does Umm al-Barahin list?
checks.why: One of existence, five negating, seven of meaning and seven that follow from them: twenty.

checks.q: What extra attribute do the Maturidis count, that the Ash'aris place under power and will?
w: Hearing: Allah's perceiving of all sounds
Mercy: Allah's kindness to His creation
checks.why: Both views are Ahl al-Sunnah. It is a difference of how to count, not of belief in Allah's perfection.

lessons.about: The full list from Umm al-Barahin, and what each group means.

cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the necessary attributes

checks.why: Existence is first: all the other attributes are of the One who exists.

checks.q: Which group are 'no beginning, no end, unlike creation, needing nothing, Oneness'?
w: The names of the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Each one denies something that does not befit Allah.

checks.q: Which is one of the seven attributes of meaning (ma'ani)?
checks.why: The seven of meaning: power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight and speech.

checks.q: 'Allah is Knowing' follows from which attribute?
checks.why: Each of the seven that follow comes from one of the seven of meaning.

checks.q: How many attributes in total are necessary for Allah, in Umm al-Barahin?
checks.why: 1 + 5 + 7 + 7 = 20. His perfection is without limit; these are what every Muslim must know in detail.

lessons.title: The Speech of Allah
lessons.about: The Qur'an is Allah's speech, not created like ours.

cards.x: Allah speaks with an eternal speech. The Qur'an is the speech of Allah: it came from Him, without asking how, and He sent it down to His Messenger ﷺ as revelation.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Qur'an

cards.x: The believers are certain it is truly Allah's speech, not created like the speech of creation. Whoever hears it and claims it is human speech has disbelieved.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Qur'an

cards.x: Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said: the Qur'an is written in the copies, preserved in the hearts and recited by the tongues. Our pronouncing, writing and reciting it are created; the Qur'an itself is not created.
cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, on the Qur'an

checks.q: What is the Qur'an, according to Imam al-Tahawi?
checks.a: The speech of Allah, not created
w: The speech of Allah, created when revealed
The words of the Prophet ﷺ, inspired by Allah
The words of Jibril, sent down to the Prophet ﷺ
checks.why: Al-Tahawi: it came from Allah and is not created like the speech of creation.

checks.q: Imam Abu Hanifah says some things about the Qur'an are created. Which?
checks.a: Our reciting and writing of it
w: The Qur'an itself, which came down in time
Allah's speech, since it is in Arabic
Its meanings, though not its words
checks.why: Our voices, ink and paper are created. The Qur'an itself, Allah's speech, is not.

checks.q: Where is the Qur'an, according to Imam Abu Hanifah in al-Fiqh al-Akbar?
checks.a: Written in copies, kept in hearts, recited by tongues
w: Only in the copies, which are its true home
Only in the hearts of those who memorise it
Only in the Preserved Tablet, not on earth
checks.why: He described it in all three ways, while it remains Allah's uncreated speech.

checks.q: Someone hears the Qur'an recited and says 'this is just human speech'. What does al-Tahawi say?
w: He is excused if he is new
checks.why: Al-Tahawi says whoever hears it and claims it is human speech has disbelieved. Allah threatened such a person with Saqar.

lessons.title: What is impossible and possible for Allah
lessons.about: The opposites of His attributes, and what He freely does.

cards.x: The opposite of every necessary attribute is impossible for Allah: non-existence, having a beginning or end, resembling creation, needing anything, having a partner, weakness, ignorance, death and so on.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is impossible for Allah

cards.x: What is possible for Allah is doing or leaving anything that is possible. Nothing obliges Him: if He rewards us it is pure bounty, and if He punishes it is pure justice.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah; Jawharat al-Tawhid

cards.x: This protects you from two mistakes: thinking Allah is like us, and thinking anything is forced upon Him.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, what is possible for Allah

checks.q: Which of these is impossible for Allah?
checks.why: Needing is the opposite of 'standing by Himself', so it is impossible for Him.

checks.q: What is possible (ja'iz) for Allah, according to al-Sanusi?
checks.a: Doing or leaving anything that is possible
w: Only what is best for creation
checks.why: He may create or not create, give or withhold. Nothing forces Him.

checks.q: Is Allah obliged to reward people for good deeds?
checks.a: No, His reward is pure bounty
w: Yes, He must reward every good deed
Yes, but only the deeds done in prayer
Only the Prophets must be rewarded
checks.why: Nothing is obligatory upon Allah. He promised reward out of generosity, and He keeps His promise.

checks.q: Allah punishes someone for their sins. Is that unjust?
checks.why: If He rewards it is bounty; if He punishes it is justice. Nothing He does is wrong.

lessons.title: The Messengers عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ
lessons.about: What is necessary, impossible and possible for the Messengers.

cards.x: The Messengers are truthful (sidq), trustworthy (amanah) and convey everything they were commanded to convey (tabligh).
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Lying, betraying trust, and hiding what they were commanded to convey are impossible for them.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them, such as eating, sleeping, marriage and illness that is not repulsive.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, on the Messengers

cards.x: Muhammad ﷺ is the last Prophet and the Messenger to all of mankind and jinn. There is no prophet after him.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on the Prophet ﷺ

checks.q: Which three qualities are necessary for every Messenger of Allah?
checks.a: Truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying the message
w: Wisdom, power and never falling ill
Trustworthiness, kingship and knowing the unseen
checks.why: Sidq (truthfulness), amanah (trustworthiness) and tabligh (conveying) are necessary for them.

checks.q: Which of these human things is possible for a Messenger?
checks.why: Human things that do not lower their rank are possible for them.

checks.q: Who is the last Prophet, after whom there is no prophet?
checks.why: He ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets. 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ will return, but as a follower of his law.

checks.q: Which is impossible for a Messenger of Allah?
checks.why: The opposites of truthfulness, trustworthiness and conveying are impossible for them.

lessons.title: Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.about: Who he is, his rank, and what we owe him.

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

Yes, 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ as a new prophet with a new law

checks.q: To whom was the Prophet ﷺ sent?

checks.q: What is the greatest miracle of the Prophet ﷺ, which remains today?

checks.q: The Prophet ﷺ said none of you truly believes until he loves him more than…

checks.q: How many prophets are named in the Qur'an?

lessons.title: The meaning of the Shahadah
lessons.about: How 'la ilaha illa Allah' gathers all of belief.

cards.x: Imam al-Sanusi ends by showing that all of belief is gathered in 'La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammadun Rasulullah'.
cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

cards.src: Umm al-Barahin, the meaning of the Shahadah

checks.q: Al-Sanusi explains 'la ilaha illa Allah' (no god but Allah). What does it mean?

Both halves equally, word for word

checks.q: How does al-Sanusi advise us to say the Shahadah?

checks.q: Why should we know the meaning of 'la ilaha illa Allah', not only say it?
checks.a: Because every belief about Allah follows from its meaning
w: Because the words alone have no reward
Because only scholars may say it
Because it must be translated before it is said
checks.why: Al-Sanusi shows that all the attributes are contained in it, so knowing it strengthens faith.

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on sin and faith

checks.a: No, unless he claims the sin is lawful

Only if he does not pray

lessons.title: What takes a person out of Islam

cards.src: al-Fiqh al-Akbar, What takes a person out of Islam

checks.a: No; it is for qualified scholars, with great caution

checks.q: Praying so that people praise you is called…

cards.x: Paradise and the Fire are created. They will never end and never perish.
cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on Paradise and the Fire

checks.q: Which two angels question a person in the grave?

They exist now, but will end after a long time
Only Paradise exists now and lasts forever

checks.a: A real pool from which he gives his Ummah to drink

A pool in Madinah in this world

checks.a: The Bridge over the Fire that people cross

The gate that leads into Paradise
The river of al-Kawthar in Paradise

checks.why: Al-Tahawi: the seeing is true for the people of Paradise, without encompassing Him and without 'how'.

checks.a: 'Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord'

'Say: He is Allah, One; Allah, the Self-Sufficient'
'Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth'

lessons.title: Allah's decree (qadr)

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on decree

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, on decree

Only the Prophets may ask about it

lessons.title: Signs of the Hour

All rain stopping for forty years

lessons.title: Prophets, saints and wonders

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, Prophets and awliya'

They are equal in rank before Allah

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the people of the qiblah

cards.src: al-'Aqidah al-Tahawiyyah, the imams and the Jama'ah; conclusion

checks.a: Any Muslim of the qiblah, righteous or sinful

Only scholars who know the sunnah well

title: Fiqh
sub: Purification, prayer, fasting, zakat and Hajj, in the Hanafi school

lessons.title: Foundations: fard, wajib and sunnah
lessons.about: The school we follow and the words fiqh uses.

cards.x: This course follows the Hanafi school of Imam Abu Hanifah al-Nu'man رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, through Nur al-Idah of Imam al-Shurunbulali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mukhtasar al-Quduri of Imam al-Quduri رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah; Mukhtasar al-Quduri

cards.x: Fard is what is established by a definitive proof with no doubt in it. You must act on it and believe in it.
cards.src: Usul al-Shashi, on fard and wajib

cards.x: Wajib is established by a proof with some doubt in it. It is like fard in action, so you may not leave it, but you are not required to believe in it with certainty as you do with fard.
cards.src: Usul al-Shashi, on fard and wajib

cards.src: Nur al-Idah; Mukhtasar al-Quduri

checks.q: Fard is established by…
checks.a: A definitive proof with no doubt in it
w: A proof with some doubt in it
The custom of the people of a town
The preference of a great scholar
checks.why: Al-Shashi: fard is what is established by a definitive proof with no doubt in it.

checks.q: Can you leave a wajib act?
checks.a: No, it is like fard in action

checks.q: How is wajib different from fard?
checks.a: Its proof has some doubt, so belief in it isn't certain
w: It is more important, so leaving it is worse

It has no reward, only a sin for leaving it
checks.why: Wajib is fard in action but not in belief, because its proof carries some doubt.

checks.q: Which ruling is closest to haram, so doing it is a sin?
checks.why: Makruh tahriman is prohibitively disliked: close to haram. Makruh tanzihan is only better left.

lessons.title: Using the toilet and istinja'
lessons.about: Cleaning yourself properly, and the manners of the toilet.

cards.x: Istinja' means cleaning the private parts after using the toilet, with water or with something like stones or tissue. Istibra' means making sure the urine has completely stopped before cleaning. Najasah means impurity, such as urine or faeces.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on istinja'

cards.x: A man must make sure the last drops of urine have stopped before he cleans himself and makes wudu, in whatever way works for him, such as walking a little, coughing or waiting. If drops come out after wudu, the wudu breaks.

cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the sunnahs of wudu

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth during wudu is…
checks.why: In wudu it is sunnah. In ghusl it is fard.

checks.q: By the sunnah, how many times is each part washed in wudu?
checks.a: Three times; the head is wiped once
w: Once; the head is wiped once
Three times; the head is wiped three times
Twice; the head is wiped once
checks.why: Once is enough for validity; three is sunnah. The head is wiped once, all of it, with the ears.

checks.q: Which of these is a sunnah of wudu?
checks.why: Starting with the right is sunnah, as is following the order and not pausing long.

lessons.title: What breaks wudu
lessons.about: What breaks wudu in the Hanafi school, and what does not.

cards.x: Anything that comes out of the front or back passage, flowing blood or pus, and vomit that fills the mouth all break wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Sleeping without being seated firmly on the ground breaks it, as do fainting, insanity and drunkenness.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Laughing out loud in a prayer with bowing and prostration breaks both the prayer and the wudu, for a sane, awake adult.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

cards.x: Touching your private part, touching a woman, blood that does not flow, vomit that does not fill the mouth, and dozing while sitting firmly do not break wudu.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Which breaks wudu in the Hanafi school?
w: A spot of blood that does not flow
checks.why: Blood that flows from the body breaks wudu. Blood that does not flow does not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Which kind of sleep breaks wudu?
checks.a: Sleep without being seated firmly on the ground
w: Sleeping in the sunnah way in prostration
A moment of drowsiness while sitting
checks.why: Sleep breaks wudu when you are not seated firmly on the ground. Dozing while seated firmly does not.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Laughing out loud during the prayer…
checks.a: Breaks both the prayer and the wudu
w: Breaks only the wudu, not the prayer
Breaks only the prayer, not the wudu
checks.why: Laughing out loud in a prayer with ruku' and sujud breaks both the prayer and the wudu.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, what breaks wudu, and what does not

checks.q: Does touching your private part break wudu in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists it among things that do not break wudu.

lessons.title: Ghusl: the full bath
lessons.about: When ghusl becomes fard and how to do it properly.

cards.x: Ghusl is washing the whole body. It becomes fard after the release of semen with desire, after intercourse even without release, and when menstruation (hayd) or post-natal bleeding (nifas) ends.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what makes ghusl necessary, and how it is done

cards.x: Rinse the whole mouth, wash inside the nose, and wash the whole body once, so that no dry spot remains, including the navel and under the beard.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what makes ghusl necessary, and how it is done

cards.x: A man must wet the inside of his plaited hair. A woman does not have to undo her plaits if water reaches the roots.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what makes ghusl necessary, and how it is done

cards.x: Wash the hands, wash off any impurity and the private parts, make wudu, then pour water over the head three times, the right side three times and the left side three times, rubbing the body.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what makes ghusl necessary, and how it is done

checks.q: What is ghusl?
checks.why: Ghusl is the full bath, needed after janabah, hayd and nifas.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, rinsing the mouth during ghusl is…
checks.why: In ghusl, rinsing the whole mouth and washing inside the nose are fard.

checks.q: Which of these makes ghusl fard?
checks.why: Ghusl is fard when hayd or nifas ends, after intercourse, and after release of semen with desire.

checks.q: For ghusl, must a woman undo her plaited hair?
checks.a: No, if water reaches the roots
checks.why: Water reaching the roots is enough.

lessons.title: Impurities and what is excused
lessons.about: Heavy and light impurity, and how much prevents prayer.

cards.x: A dirham was a silver coin. In this chapter it is a measure. For liquid impurity it is an area: the hollow of your palm when you cup it, roughly 3 cm across, about the size of a 2p coin. For solid impurity it is a weight of 20 qirats (a mithqal), a few grams.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, types of impurity

cards.x: Heavy (ghalizah) impurities include wine, flowing blood, urine of animals that are not eaten, dog and predator droppings, and anything from the human body that breaks wudu when it comes out.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, types of impurity

cards.x: Light (khafifah) impurities include the urine of a horse or of animals that are eaten, and droppings of birds that are not eaten.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, types of impurity

cards.x: Up to the size of a dirham of heavy impurity is excused, and less than a quarter of a garment or limb of light impurity. Tiny splashes of urine like pinheads are excused too.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what is excused

checks.q: In this chapter a dirham is a measure. How big is it for liquid impurity?
checks.a: The hollow of the palm, about 3 cm across
w: The whole hand, open and flat
A single drop, the size of a pea
checks.why: For liquid impurity it is an area: the cupped palm, roughly a 2p coin. For solid impurity it is a weight.

checks.q: Heavy impurity (like urine or flowing blood) on your clothes: how much is excused in prayer?
checks.a: Up to the size of a dirham
checks.why: Up to a dirham is excused, though washing it is still better.

checks.q: Flowing blood is which kind of impurity?
checks.why: Flowing blood is listed among the heavy impurities.

checks.q: Light impurity (like the urine of animals that are eaten) is excused if it is…
checks.a: Less than a quarter of the garment or limb
w: Less than a dirham, like heavy impurity
Any amount, as long as it is dry
checks.why: Light impurity has a wider allowance: less than a quarter.

lessons.title: Tayammum: when there is no water
lessons.about: When you may use earth instead of water, and how.

cards.x: Tayammum is purifying with clean earth when water cannot be used. It is allowed when you are a mile or more from water (a Hanafi mile is about 1.8 km), when using water would make you ill or worse, when it is dangerously cold, or when you need the water to drink.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on tayammum

cards.x: Make the intention, strike clean earth with both palms and wipe the whole face; strike again and wipe both arms including the elbows.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on tayammum

cards.x: Tayammum stands in place of wudu and ghusl. It ends when water becomes available and you are able to use it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on tayammum

checks.q: What is tayammum?
checks.a: Purifying with clean earth when water can't be used
w: Making wudu with very little water
Wiping over socks instead of washing
Washing only the face and hands
checks.why: Tayammum stands in place of wudu and ghusl when water cannot be used.

checks.q: You can't find water. How far away must it be for tayammum to be allowed?
checks.a: A mile or more, about 1.8 km
w: Any distance, if you are tired
checks.why: A Hanafi mile is 4,000 cubits, about 1.8 km.

checks.q: In tayammum, how many times are the hands struck on the earth?
checks.a: Twice: once for the face, once for the arms
w: Once: for the face and arms together
Three times: face, arms, then feet
Twice: once for the face, once for the feet
checks.why: Strike, wipe the face; strike again, wipe both arms with the elbows.

checks.q: What ends tayammum, besides what breaks wudu?
checks.a: Finding water you are able to use
w: The next prayer time coming in
Nothing ends it until you sleep
checks.why: It stands in place of water only until water can be used.

lessons.title: Wiping over leather socks (khuffs)
lessons.about: When you may wipe, for how long, and how.

cards.x: Khuffs are leather socks that cover the ankles. If you put them on while in wudu, then later make wudu again, you may wipe over them with wet hands instead of washing your feet, for a set time.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time limit for wiping

cards.x: A resident wipes for one day and night, a traveller for three days and nights. The time starts from the first thing that breaks wudu after putting them on.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time limit for wiping

cards.x: Put them on after washing the feet, in wudu. They must cover the ankles, be strong enough to walk in, and have no hole the size of three small toes.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, conditions for wiping

cards.x: The fard is wiping the top of the front of each foot, the size of three of the hand's small fingers. The sunnah is drawing spread fingers from the toes up towards the shin.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the amount that is fard

checks.q: What are khuffs?
w: A cloth wrapped round the feet
checks.why: If put on while in wudu, you may wipe over them instead of washing your feet, for a set time.

checks.q: How long may a traveller wipe over leather socks (khuffs)?
checks.why: A resident wipes one day and night; a traveller three.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), when does the time limit start?
checks.a: From the first thing that breaks wudu after wearing them
w: From the moment you put them on in wudu
From the next Fajr after putting them on
From the first time you wipe over them
checks.why: Put them on in wudu at Fajr, and your wudu breaks at noon: the count starts at noon.

checks.q: When wiping over leather socks (khuffs), what is the least you must wipe?
checks.a: Three fingers' width on the top of each foot
w: The whole sock, top and bottom
checks.why: The fard is the size of three of the hand's small fingers on the top front of each foot.

lessons.title: Menstruation and post-natal bleeding
lessons.about: Its length and what is not allowed during it.

cards.x: Hayd is menstruation, the monthly period. Nifas is the bleeding after giving birth. The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it can end after a day.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on menstruation

cards.x: During menstruation and nifas: prayer, fasting, reciting a verse of the Qur'an, touching the Qur'an without a cover, entering a masjid, tawaf, and intercourse.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, what menstruation forbids

cards.x: She makes up the fasts she missed, but not the prayers.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, making up the obligations

cards.x: Bleeding shorter than three days, longer than ten, or beyond forty after birth is istihadah (irregular bleeding). It does not stop prayer or fasting: she makes wudu for each prayer time and prays.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, chapter on menstruation

checks.q: What is nifas?
w: Bleeding from a cut or wound
checks.why: Nifas is post-natal bleeding. Hayd is the monthly period.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the longest a period (hayd) can last?
checks.why: The shortest hayd is three days and the longest ten. Bleeding beyond that is not hayd.

checks.q: What is the longest nifas (bleeding after giving birth) can last?
checks.why: Nifas is at most forty days, with no minimum: it may end after a day.

checks.q: After her period, what does a woman make up?
checks.why: She makes up missed fasts. Missed prayers are forgiven, a mercy from Allah.

lessons.title: The five prayer times
lessons.about: When each prayer starts and ends, and the forbidden times.

cards.x: Fajr is from true dawn (when light spreads across the horizon) until just before sunrise. Zuhr is from when the sun passes its highest point until an object's shadow is twice its length (once, in the view of the two companions), not counting its midday shadow.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the prayer times

cards.x: 'Asr is from the end of Zuhr until sunset. Maghrib is from sunset until the red twilight disappears. 'Isha' and witr are from then until dawn; witr is not prayed before 'Isha'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the prayer times

cards.x: No fard or wajib prayer owed from before is valid at sunrise until the sun rises, when it is at its height, and when it turns yellow until it sets. Voluntary prayer is prohibitively disliked then.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Fajr end?
w: At the first light of dawn
checks.why: Fajr lasts from true dawn until just before the sun rises.

checks.q: When does Maghrib end in the Hanafi fatwa?
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: until the red twilight is gone, on the view the fatwa follows.

checks.q: Which is a time when prayer is not valid?
w: In the middle of the night
checks.why: Sunrise, the sun's height and its setting are the three forbidden times.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the times when prayer is not valid

checks.q: When does the time of Maghrib end?
checks.why: Maghrib lasts from sunset until the redness in the sky has gone; then 'Isha' begins.

lessons.title: The adhan and iqamah
lessons.about: Their ruling and their words.

cards.x: The adhan and iqamah are a stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men, whether praying alone or in a group, at home or travelling, on time or making up.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' four times at the start, then each phrase twice, ending with 'Allahu akbar' twice and 'La ilaha illa Allah'. The iqamah is the same.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

cards.x: Allahu akbar: Allah is the Greatest. Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah: I bear witness there is no god but Allah. Ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah: I bear witness Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Hayya 'ala al-salah: come to prayer. Hayya 'ala al-falah: come to success. La ilaha illa Allah: there is no god but Allah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of the adhan and iqamah

cards.x: In the adhan of Fajr add 'al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm' (prayer is better than sleep) twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah'. In the iqamah add 'qad qamat al-salah' (the prayer has begun) twice. Give the adhan slowly and the iqamah quickly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the adhan is given

checks.q: What does 'hayya 'ala al-falah' in the adhan mean?
checks.why: 'Hayya 'ala al-salah' is 'come to prayer'; 'hayya 'ala al-falah' is 'come to success'.

checks.q: What is the ruling of the adhan for a fard prayer?
checks.why: A stressed sunnah for every fard prayer, for men.

checks.q: In the adhan of Fajr, what is added, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Al-salatu khayrun min al-nawm': prayer is better than sleep
w: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
'Hayya 'ala al-falah': come to success, said four times
'Allahu akbar': Allah is the Greatest, said six times
checks.why: It is said twice after 'hayya 'ala al-falah', reminding the sleeper.

checks.q: What is added in the iqamah, and what does it mean?
checks.a: 'Qad qamat al-salah': the prayer has begun
checks.why: The iqamah is said just before the prayer starts, and said quickly.

lessons.title: Before you pray
lessons.about: The conditions that must be in place before your prayer starts.

cards.x: You must be in wudu (and ghusl if needed), and your body, clothes and the place you pray on must be clean of impurity.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: The 'awrah is the part of the body that must be covered. In prayer, for a man it is from the navel to below the knees. For a woman it is the whole body except the face, the hands and the feet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Face the qiblah, pray after the time has come in, and intend the prayer you are praying, such as today's Zuhr.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

cards.x: Begin with 'Allahu akbar' while standing, saying it so that you hear yourself.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the conditions of the prayer

checks.q: In prayer, the 'awrah (what must be covered) for a man is…
checks.a: From the navel to below the knees
w: From the chest to the ankles
The whole body except the face
checks.why: A man's 'awrah is from the navel to below the knees; a woman's is all but the face, hands and feet.

checks.q: You pray Zuhr before its time has come in. Is it valid?
checks.a: No, the time must have come in
w: Yes, if you did not know
checks.why: A prayer before its time is not valid; pray it again once the time comes in.

checks.q: Which of these is a condition for the prayer to be valid?
checks.a: A clean body, clothes and place
w: Praying in a masjid, in congregation
Praying at the start of the time
checks.why: Purity of body, clothes and place, covering the 'awrah, facing the qiblah, the time and the intention.

lessons.title: The pillars of prayer
lessons.about: The parts of the prayer it cannot be valid without.

cards.x: Inside the prayer, four things are pillars: standing, reciting, bowing (ruku') and prostrating (sujud).
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: Nur al-Idah names these four, then adds that the final sitting, for as long as it takes to recite the tashahhud, is also said to be a pillar. Either way it is fard: the prayer is not valid without it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

cards.x: If a pillar is missed, the prayer is not valid and must be prayed again. The prostration of forgetfulness cannot fix it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the pillars of the prayer

checks.q: Which of these is a pillar (fard part) inside the prayer?
w: Placing the right hand over the left
checks.why: The pillars inside the prayer: standing, reciting, ruku' and sujud, and the final sitting.

checks.q: You missed a pillar of the prayer, like a sujud. What do you do?
checks.a: Pray it again; it is not valid
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it
checks.why: A missing pillar cannot be repaired by sajdat al-sahw.

checks.q: How long must the final sitting of the prayer be, at least?
checks.why: The final sitting is fard for at least the length of the tashahhud.

lessons.title: The wajib acts of prayer
lessons.about: The wajib acts, and what to do if you miss one.

cards.x: Wajib acts include: reciting al-Fatihah, adding a surah or three verses, calmness in every position, the first sitting, the tashahhud, and ending with 'al-salam'.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act by mistake, make two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw) at the end, with tashahhud and salam.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

cards.x: If you leave a wajib act deliberately, you are sinful and must repeat the prayer.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is…
w: Recommended only in the first rak'ah
checks.why: In the Hanafi school, reciting al-Fatihah is wajib, not a pillar.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You forgot the first sitting. What do you do?
checks.a: Make the two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end
w: Start the prayer again straight away
checks.why: The first sitting is wajib. Leaving it by mistake is fixed with two prostrations of forgetfulness at the end.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: You left a wajib act on purpose. What follows?
checks.a: You are sinful and must repeat the prayer
w: Two prostrations of forgetfulness fix it
Nothing, if it was a small act
checks.why: Leaving a wajib act on purpose is sinful, and the prayer must be repeated.
checks.src: Nur al-Idah, the wajib acts, and the prostration of forgetfulness

checks.q: Which of these is wajib in prayer, not a pillar?
checks.why: In the Hanafi school reciting is a pillar, but al-Fatihah in particular is wajib.

lessons.title: How to pray (1): from takbir to ruku'
lessons.about: The prayer step by step, as Nur al-Idah describes it.

cards.x: Raise the hands to the ears (a woman to her shoulders) and say 'Allahu akbar', intending the prayer. A man places his right hand over his left below the navel; a woman places them on her chest.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Say the opening praise: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bi-hamdika, wa tabaraka ismuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk.' Then seek refuge (a'udhu billah) and say bismillah quietly.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Recite al-Fatihah, say 'amin' quietly, then a surah or three verses.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Say 'Allahu akbar' and bow, back straight with the head level with it, holding the knees with fingers spread. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-'azim' three times, the least of the sunnah.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

checks.q: Where does a man place his hands after the takbir?
checks.a: Right over left, below the navel
w: Right over left, on the chest
Left over right, below the navel
checks.why: Nur al-Idah: right over left below the navel for a man; a woman places them on her chest.

checks.q: What is said straight after the opening takbir?
checks.why: The opening praise (thana') comes first, then ta'awwudh and bismillah.

checks.q: How many times is the tasbih of ruku' said at least, by the sunnah?
checks.why: Three times is the least of the sunnah.

checks.q: Where does a man place his hands while standing in prayer?
checks.a: Right over left, below the navel
w: Right over left, on the chest
Left over right, on the chest
checks.why: A man places them below the navel; a woman places them on her chest.

lessons.title: How to pray (2): from rising to salam
lessons.about: Prostration, sitting, tashahhud and ending the prayer.

cards.x: Rise saying 'Sami' Allahu li-man hamidah, rabbana laka al-hamd' (a follower says only the second part), and stand still for a moment.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: Go down with 'Allahu akbar', placing knees, then hands, then face between the hands, nose and forehead on the ground. Say 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' three times. Sit calmly, then make the second sujud the same way.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, how the prayer is put together

cards.x: After the second rak'ah, sit on the left foot with the right foot upright, hands on the thighs, and recite the tashahhud: 'Al-tahiyyatu lillahi wa al-salawatu wa al-tayyibat…'
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, how to pray

cards.x: In the final sitting, after the tashahhud send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a in words like the Qur'an and the reported supplications. Then say 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah' to the right and to the left.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, how to pray

checks.q: Which touches the ground first when going into sujud?
checks.why: Knees, then hands, then the face.

checks.q: What does a follower say when rising from ruku'?
checks.why: The imam or one praying alone says both; the follower says only the praise.

checks.q: What comes after the tashahhud in the final sitting?
checks.a: Blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then du'a, then salam
w: Salam straight away, then du'a afterwards
Du'a, then blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then salam
Another sujud, then blessings, then salam
checks.why: Al-Quduri: tashahhud, blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, du'a, then salam right and left.

checks.q: What is said three times in sujud?
checks.why: 'Subhana rabbiya al-a'la' (glory to my Lord, the Most High) in sujud; 'al-'azim' (the Magnificent) is said in ruku'.

lessons.title: Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer
lessons.about: What perfects the prayer, and what spoils its beauty.

cards.x: Raising the hands at the opening takbir, the opening praise (thana'), seeking refuge, bismillah, 'amin', the takbirs when moving, the glorifications in ruku' and sujud, and blessings on the Prophet ﷺ in the last sitting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

cards.x: Playing with clothes or body, cracking the fingers, looking around, hands on the hips, yawning without covering the mouth, closing the eyes without need, and praying while needing the toilet.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

cards.x: It is disliked to pray facing a picture of a living being, on a path, in a bathroom, or with someone's face turned towards you.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, Sunnahs and dislikes of prayer

checks.q: Which of these is a sunnah of prayer?
checks.why: Al-Fatihah is wajib, the final sitting is fard, facing the qiblah is a condition; 'amin' is sunnah.

checks.q: You need the toilet badly as the prayer starts. What is best?
checks.a: Use the toilet first, then pray
checks.why: Praying while holding it in is disliked, as it takes away humility.

checks.q: Which of these is disliked in prayer?
w: Looking at the place of sujud
Keeping the feet apart a little
checks.why: The eyes stay on the place of sujud while standing.

checks.q: Is it disliked to pray facing a picture of a living being?
w: Only if it is a photo
checks.why: Nur al-Idah lists it among what is disliked.

lessons.title: The prostration of forgetfulness
lessons.about: How to fix a mistake in prayer.

cards.x: Sajdat al-sahw, the prostration of forgetfulness, is two extra prostrations at the end of the prayer that repair a mistake, such as forgetting the first sitting.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, sujud al-sahw: its ruling

cards.x: Two prostrations, with tashahhud and salam, become wajib when a wajib act of the prayer is left out by mistake, even if it happens more than once.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, sujud al-sahw: its ruling

cards.x: The sunnah is to do it after the salam: give one salam to the right, make the two sujud, then sit for tashahhud and end with salam. Doing it before salam is mildly disliked.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the time of the prostration

cards.x: If a wajib act is left on purpose, the person is sinful and the prayer must be repeated; the prostration of forgetfulness does not fix it.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, leaving a wajib on purpose

checks.q: What is sajdat al-sahw?

cards.x: Two rak'ahs before Fajr (the most important), four before Zuhr and two after, two after Maghrib, two after 'Isha', and four before Jumu'ah and four after it.

cards.src: Nur al-Idah, The regular sunnah prayers

checks.q: Which is the most important sunnah prayer?

checks.q: How many stressed sunnah rak'ahs are there before Zuhr?

checks.why: Two stressed rak'ahs after Maghrib.

lessons.title: The traveller's prayer

cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of shortening

cards.x: He keeps shortening until he returns home or intends to stay fifteen days or more in one town. If he intends less, or does not know when he will leave, he keeps shortening even for years.

checks.q: Which prayers does a traveller shorten?
checks.why: They become two rak'ahs. Fajr and Maghrib stay as they are.

checks.q: How far must a journey be for prayers to be shortened?

checks.why: Intending fifteen days or more in one town ends the travel ruling.

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, is shortening the prayer while travelling optional?
checks.why: Shortening is 'azimah (the rule), not just a permission.

lessons.title: Making up missed prayers

cards.src: Nur al-Idah, making up missed prayers

cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the ruling of order

cards.x: Leaving a prayer deliberately out of laziness is so serious that the jurists set a punishment for it in an Islamic state. Make up what you missed, and repent.
cards.src: Nur al-Idah, the one who leaves the prayer

checks.why: A prayer is made up as it was missed: two for a traveller.

checks.a: Yes, while you owe fewer than six

checks.q: What happens to a prayer that was missed?
checks.a: It stays owed and must be made up
w: It is forgiven if you repent

lessons.title: The Jumu'ah prayer

lessons.title: Qurbani (udhiyah)
lessons.about: The sacrifice of Eid al-Adha: who must give it, and how.

cards.x: In the Hanafi school, the qurbani is wajib on a free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab beyond their basic needs on the days of sacrifice. It is for oneself, not for one's children.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Qurbani (udhiyah)

cards.x: From after the Eid prayer on the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah until sunset on the 12th. Where there is no Eid prayer, from dawn on the 10th.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Qurbani (udhiyah)

cards.x: A sheep or goat of at least one year counts for one person. A cow (two years) or a camel (five years) counts for up to seven people, each with a full share. It must be free of major defects.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Qurbani (udhiyah)

cards.x: It is recommended to divide it into thirds: for your family, for relatives and friends, and for the poor. The skin may be given away but not sold.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Qurbani (udhiyah)

checks.q: In the Hanafi school, what is the ruling of qurbani for someone who owns the nisab?
checks.why: Wajib on the free, resident Muslim who owns the nisab on the days of sacrifice.

checks.q: How many people can share one cow for qurbani?
checks.why: A cow or camel counts for up to seven; a sheep or goat for one.

checks.q: When may the qurbani be slaughtered?
checks.a: After the Eid prayer on the 10th until sunset on the 12th
checks.why: Slaughtering before the Eid prayer, where it is held, does not count.

checks.q: How old must a goat be for qurbani?
checks.why: A sheep of six months that looks like a yearling is also accepted.

lessons.title: Who must perform Hajj
lessons.about: The conditions, and the months of Hajj.

cards.x: Hajj is fard on free, adult, sane and healthy Muslims who can afford the provision and transport, beyond their home, their needs and their family's maintenance until they return, when the road is safe.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: A woman must have a mahram or her husband with her if Makkah is three days' journey or more away. She may not go for Hajj without one of them.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Tamattu'

checks.q: Hajj is fard on someone who…
checks.a: Can afford travel beyond his needs and his family's upkeep
w: Has any savings at all, even if he is in debt
Can afford the travel, even if his family is left in need
Has already done 'umrah and lives near Makkah
checks.why: Al-Quduri ties it to affording provision and transport beyond needs and family maintenance, with a safe road.

checks.q: Can a woman go for Hajj without a mahram or husband, from far away?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she may not perform Hajj without a mahram or husband if the journey is three days or more.

checks.q: Which are the months of Hajj?
checks.a: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
w: Only the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah
Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram
checks.why: Al-Quduri defines them in the chapter on tamattu'.

checks.q: May a woman travel for Hajj without a mahram or her husband?
checks.a: No, if Makkah is three days' journey or more
w: Yes, in a group of women
Yes, if she has the money
checks.why: Al-Quduri makes a mahram or husband a condition for her, from that distance.

lessons.title: The miqat and entering ihram
lessons.about: Where to enter ihram, and how.

cards.x: Do not pass these without ihram: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah, Dhat 'Irq for Iraq, al-Juhfah for Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for Najd, and Yalamlam for Yemen. Entering ihram before them is allowed.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the miqats

cards.x: Make ghusl (or wudu, but ghusl is better), put on two clean sheets, a lower and an upper one, apply perfume if you have it, and pray two rak'ahs.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Say: 'O Allah, I intend Hajj, make it easy for me and accept it from me.' Then say the talbiyah: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak.' With the talbiyah you are in ihram.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

checks.q: What is the miqat for people coming from Madinah?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: Dhu al-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah.

checks.q: When do you actually enter ihram?
checks.a: When you say the talbiyah with the intention
w: When you put on the two sheets
When you first see the Ka'bah
checks.why: 'When he says the talbiyah, he has entered ihram.'

checks.q: Before ihram, which is better?
checks.why: Ghusl or wudu, and ghusl is better.

checks.q: When do you actually enter ihram?
checks.a: With the intention and the talbiyah
w: When you put on the two sheets
When you first see the Ka'bah
checks.why: The sheets, ghusl and two rak'ahs prepare you; the intention with the talbiyah makes you muhrim.

lessons.title: What ihram forbids
lessons.about: What the muhrim must avoid.

cards.x: Avoid intimacy and its talk, sinning and arguing. Do not hunt, or point out or direct anyone to game.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: A man does not wear a shirt, trousers, turban, cap, cloak or khuffs (unless he has no sandals, then he cuts them below the ankles), and does not cover his head or face.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Do not use perfume, shave the head or body hair, trim the beard or cut the nails. Bathing, shade and wearing a money belt are allowed.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: A woman is like a man in all this, except that she covers her head and uncovers her face, does not raise her voice in the talbiyah, does not jog in tawaf or run between the green markers, and trims her hair instead of shaving.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

checks.q: May a man in ihram cover his head?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: he does not cover his head or face.

checks.q: Which is allowed in ihram?
checks.why: Bathing, shade and a money belt are allowed.

checks.q: In ihram, a woman…
checks.a: Covers her head and uncovers her face
w: Uncovers her head and covers her face
Covers both her head and face
Shaves her head at the end
checks.why: She keeps her head covered and her face uncovered.

lessons.title: The three ways of Hajj
lessons.about: Ifrad, tamattu' and qiran.

cards.x: Entering ihram for Hajj alone.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Entering ihram for 'umrah in the months of Hajj, completing it and leaving ihram, then entering ihram for Hajj from Makkah on the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah). A sacrifice is due; if you cannot, fast three days during Hajj and seven when you return.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Tamattu'

cards.x: Entering ihram for 'umrah and Hajj together from the miqat. In the Hanafi school qiran is the best, then tamattu', then ifrad. It too requires a sacrifice.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Qiran

cards.x: The people of Makkah do not do tamattu' or qiran; only ifrad.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Tamattu'

checks.q: Which way of Hajj is best in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: qiran is better than tamattu' and ifrad.

checks.q: In tamattu', when do you enter ihram for Hajj?
checks.a: On the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, from Makkah
w: On the 10th, after the Eid prayer
checks.why: After completing the 'umrah you stay in Makkah and enter ihram for Hajj on Yawm al-Tarwiyah.

checks.q: A mutamatti' who cannot afford the sacrifice…
checks.a: Fasts three days in Hajj and seven at home
w: Fasts ten days, all in Makkah
checks.why: Three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.

lessons.title: 'Umrah
lessons.about: Its ruling and its acts.

cards.x: 'Umrah is a sunnah. It can be done at any time of year, but is disliked on five days: the day of 'Arafah, the day of sacrifice and the three days of tashriq.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: 'Umrah is: ihram, tawaf, sa'y, and shaving or trimming.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on missing Hajj

cards.x: The one in 'umrah stops the talbiyah when he starts the tawaf.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on Tamattu'

checks.q: What is the ruling of 'umrah in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'umrah is sunnah.

checks.q: On which day is 'umrah disliked?
checks.why: It is disliked on 'Arafah, the day of sacrifice and the days of tashriq.

checks.q: What are the acts of 'umrah?
checks.a: Ihram, tawaf, sa'y, then shaving or trimming
checks.why: Al-Quduri lists exactly these.

lessons.title: Tawaf and sa'y
lessons.about: Arriving in Makkah.

cards.x: Enter al-Masjid al-Haram. On seeing the House say takbir and tahlil. Begin at the Black Stone: face it, say takbir, raise your hands and touch and kiss it if you can without harming anyone.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Go round the House seven times, with the Ka'bah on your left, outside the Hatim. Men uncover the right shoulder (idtiba') and jog (raml) in the first three circuits, then walk. Touch the Stone each time you pass it if you can, and end with it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Pray two rak'ahs at the Station of Ibrahim, or wherever is easy in the masjid.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Go to al-Safa, face the House, say takbir and tahlil, send blessings on the Prophet ﷺ and make du'a. Walk to al-Marwah, men running between the two green markers. That is one circuit; complete seven, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

checks.q: Where does each circuit of tawaf begin?
w: At the door of the Ka'bah
checks.why: Al-Quduri: begin at the Black Stone.

checks.q: In which circuits do men jog (raml)?
checks.why: Raml is in the first three circuits.

checks.q: Sa'y starts at… and ends at…
checks.why: Seven circuits, starting at al-Safa and ending at al-Marwah.

lessons.title: Mina, 'Arafah and Muzdalifah
lessons.about: The 8th and 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

cards.x: On the 8th (Yawm al-Tarwiyah), after Fajr in Makkah, go to Mina and stay until you pray Fajr on the day of 'Arafah.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: The standing at 'Arafah is the heart of Hajj. Whoever is at 'Arafah at any time from midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th has caught the Hajj. All of 'Arafah is a place of standing except Batn 'Uranah. Strive in du'a.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: After sunset, leave calmly for Muzdalifah. Pray Maghrib and 'Isha' there together. After Fajr, stand and make du'a, then leave for Mina before sunrise.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

checks.q: When is the time for standing at 'Arafah?
checks.a: From midday on the 9th until dawn on the 10th
w: From sunset on the 9th until midnight
checks.why: Al-Quduri: from the sun's decline on the day of 'Arafah to dawn on the day of sacrifice.

checks.q: Where are Maghrib and 'Isha' prayed on the night of the 9th?
checks.why: Praying Maghrib on the road is not valid in the view of Abu Hanifah and Muhammad.

checks.q: Which part of 'Arafah is not a place of standing?
checks.why: All of 'Arafah is valid except Batn 'Uranah.

checks.q: What is the heart of Hajj, without which it is missed?
checks.why: 'Hajj is 'Arafah.' Whoever is there between midday on the 9th and dawn on the 10th has caught it.

lessons.title: The Day of Sacrifice and after
lessons.about: Stoning, sacrifice, shaving and tawaf al-ziyarah.

cards.x: On the 10th, stone Jamrat al-'Aqabah with seven pebbles, saying takbir with each. Stop the talbiyah with the first pebble.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Then sacrifice, then shave or trim; shaving is better. Now everything is lawful except intimacy.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Go to Makkah on the 10th, 11th or 12th and perform tawaf al-ziyarah, seven circuits. This is the fard tawaf of Hajj. After it, intimacy becomes lawful. Delaying it past these days requires a sacrifice, according to Abu Hanifah.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Return to Mina. On the 11th and 12th, after midday, stone the three jamarat, starting with the one nearest the Masjid al-Khayf, seven pebbles each, stopping to make du'a after the first two. You may leave on the 12th or stay for the 13th.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

checks.q: Which jamrah is stoned on the 10th?
checks.why: On the day of sacrifice only Jamrat al-'Aqabah is stoned.

checks.q: What is the fard tawaf of Hajj?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'This tawaf is the one that is fard in Hajj.'

checks.q: After stoning, sacrificing and shaving, what remains forbidden until tawaf al-ziyarah?
checks.why: Everything becomes lawful except intimacy, which becomes lawful after tawaf al-ziyarah.

lessons.title: Farewell, and the wajibs of Hajj
lessons.about: Tawaf al-Wada', and what a sacrifice repairs.

cards.x: Before leaving Makkah, perform tawaf al-sadr (the farewell tawaf), seven circuits without jogging. It is wajib, except for the people of Makkah. A woman who gets her period after tawaf al-ziyarah may leave without it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hajj

cards.x: Leaving sa'y, the standing at Muzdalifah, the stoning, or the farewell tawaf requires a sheep, and the Hajj is still complete.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

cards.x: Missing the standing at 'Arafah means the Hajj is missed. Tawaf al-ziyarah must be done; a sacrifice cannot replace it.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, chapter on the violations of the muhrim

checks.q: Someone left out sa'y. What follows?
checks.a: A sheep is due; the Hajj is complete
w: The Hajj is invalid and must be repeated
Nothing is due; the Hajj is complete
He fasts three days; the Hajj is complete
checks.why: Al-Quduri: 'Whoever leaves the sa'y owes a sheep, and his Hajj is complete.'

checks.q: Is the farewell tawaf wajib on the people of Makkah?
checks.why: It is wajib except on the people of Makkah.

checks.q: A woman's period starts after tawaf al-ziyarah. Before leaving she…
checks.a: May leave without the farewell tawaf
w: Must wait until she is pure
checks.why: Al-Quduri: she leaves, and owes nothing for missing tawaf al-sadr.

title: Halal & Haram
sub: Food, dress, the gaze and earning, and the levels of carefulness

lessons.title: Why halal matters
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali on the lawful and the unlawful.

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is good and accepts only what is good. He mentioned a traveller, dishevelled and dusty, raising his hands: 'O Lord!', while his food, drink and clothing are haram. 'How can he be answered?'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim; quoted in Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful

cards.x: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ opens this book with the virtue of the lawful and the blame of the unlawful, bringing verses and hadiths on how what we consume affects our worship.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Lawful and Unlawful

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said: the halal is clear and the haram is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and honour.
cards.src: Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim (al-Nawawi's Forty, 6)

checks.q: Why was the traveller's du'a not answered?
checks.a: His food, drink and clothing were haram
w: He did not raise his hands high enough
He was travelling and in a hurry
checks.why: In the hadith, the reason given is that his food, drink and clothing were haram.

checks.q: Between clear halal and clear haram are…
checks.why: Between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know.

checks.q: Avoiding doubtful things protects…
checks.why: 'Whoever avoids the doubtful has protected his religion and his honour.'

lessons.title: The major sins
lessons.about: What every Muslim must avoid.

cards.x: Major sins (kaba'ir) are those Allah threatened with the Fire, curse or a set punishment. Avoiding them is fard; Allah promises to forgive the minor sins of those who avoid the major ones.
cards.src: Qur'an, al-Nisa' 31

cards.x: Shirk, killing unjustly, magic, leaving the prayer, withholding zakat, disobeying parents, zina, drinking alcohol, riba, consuming an orphan's wealth, false witness, slandering chaste people, and fleeing the battlefield.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Wills

cards.x: Backbiting (saying what a person would dislike, even if true), carrying tales, and lying are major sins too. They are easy on the tongue and heavy on the Scale.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of the Banes of the Tongue

checks.q: What does Allah promise those who avoid the major sins?
w: That they will never be tested
checks.why: 'If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your lesser sins.' (al-Nisa' 31)

checks.q: Saying something true about a person that they would dislike is…
checks.why: If it is true it is backbiting; if false it is slander, which is worse.

checks.q: Which of these is a major sin?
w: Eating with the left hand by mistake
checks.why: The Prophet ﷺ counted disobeying parents among the greatest sins.

checks.q: Leaving the prayer out of laziness is…
checks.why: It is among the gravest sins; make it up and repent.

lessons.title: Rights of parents and family
lessons.about: Kindness to parents and keeping ties of kinship.

cards.x: Allah joined thanks to Him with thanks to parents. Obey them in everything that is not sin, speak to them gently, never say even 'uff', serve them, and pray for them, in life and after death.
cards.src: Qur'an, al-Isra' 23–24

cards.x: A man asked who most deserves his good company. The Prophet ﷺ said: your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Manners

cards.x: Keeping ties with relatives (silat al-rahim) is wajib, and cutting them is a major sin. Visit, help and keep in touch with them, even if they do not do the same.
cards.src: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Manners

checks.q: Your parents tell you to do something sinful. What do you do?
checks.a: Refuse gently, and keep being kind to them
checks.why: No obedience to anyone in disobeying Allah, but you stay kind and respectful.

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ name three times as most deserving of good company?
checks.why: Your mother, your mother, your mother, then your father.

checks.q: What is the ruling of keeping ties with relatives?
checks.a: Wajib, and cutting them is a major sin
w: Only with those who are kind to you
checks.why: Keep ties even with those who cut you off.

lessons.title: The four degrees of carefulness
lessons.about: Al-Ghazali's levels of wara'.

cards.x: The first degree, of the upright, is avoiding what the fatwa says is haram. The second, of the righteous, is also avoiding what is doubtful.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The third, of the God-fearing, is leaving some things that are fine for fear they lead to what is not.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

cards.x: The fourth, of the siddiqin, is leaving even what is harmless if it is taken for other than Allah, or not to gain strength for His worship.
cards.src: Ihya', Book of the Lawful and Unlawful, the degrees of wara'

checks.q: Avoiding what the fatwa calls haram is the wara' of…
checks.why: The first degree, required of everyone, is the wara' of the upright.

checks.q: Leaving harmless things done for other than Allah is the wara' of…
checks.why: Al-Ghazali calls this highest degree the wara' of the siddiqin.

checks.q: How many degrees of wara' does al-Ghazali give?
checks.why: He describes four: of the upright, the righteous, the God-fearing and the siddiqin.

lessons.title: Food and slaughter
lessons.about: What may be eaten, and whose slaughter is lawful.

cards.x: The slaughter of a Muslim or of a Jew or Christian (Ahl al-Kitab) is halal. The slaughter of a Magian, an apostate or an idol-worshipper is not eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: If the one slaughtering leaves out Allah's name on purpose, the animal is carrion and may not be eaten. If he forgot, it may be eaten.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

cards.x: Of sea creatures, only fish are eaten in the Hanafi school, and a fish that died by itself and floats is disliked. Locusts may be eaten without slaughter.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of Hunting and Slaughter

checks.q: Is meat slaughtered by a Christian halal?
checks.a: Yes, the slaughter of Ahl al-Kitab is halal
w: No, only a Muslim's slaughter is halal
Only if a Muslim watches him
checks.why: Al-Quduri: the slaughter of a Muslim or a Kitabi is halal.

checks.q: The slaughterer forgot to say bismillah. The meat…
checks.why: Leaving it out by forgetting does not make it haram; leaving it on purpose does.

checks.q: Which sea creatures may be eaten in the Hanafi school?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: of water animals, only fish are eaten.

lessons.title: Gold, silk and vessels
lessons.about: What men and women may wear and use.

cards.x: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, and it is lawful for women.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Men may not wear gold or silver, except a silver ring, a belt fitting and a sword decoration of silver. Women may wear gold and silver.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: Eating, drinking, oiling and perfuming from vessels of gold and silver is not allowed, for men or women. Glass and crystal are fine.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: May a man wear a gold ring?
w: Yes, if it is a wedding ring
checks.why: Men may not wear gold; a silver ring is allowed.

checks.q: Drinking from a silver cup is…
checks.a: Not allowed for men or women
checks.why: Eating and drinking from gold and silver vessels is not allowed for either.

checks.q: Wearing silk is lawful for…
checks.why: Silk is not lawful for men to wear, and lawful for women.

lessons.title: Lowering the gaze
lessons.about: What may be looked at, according to al-Quduri.

cards.x: A man may not look at a woman who is not his mahram except at her face and hands. If he is not safe from desire, he does not look even at her face, except for a need.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as their work requires.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

cards.x: A man may look at another man except between the navel and the knee.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Book of the Forbidden and the Permitted

checks.q: If a man fears desire, may he look at a non-mahram's face?
checks.why: Al-Quduri: if he is not safe from desire he does not look even at her face, except for a need.

checks.q: Which part of a man may another man not look at?
checks.a: Between the navel and the knee
w: Only between the navel and the chest
checks.why: Between the navel and the knee is 'awrah for men.

checks.q: Who may look as their work requires?
checks.why: A judge, a witness and a doctor may look as needed.

lessons.title: Riba (interest)
lessons.about: What riba is, and why it is so serious.

cards.x: Riba is haram. The Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, the one who writes it and its two witnesses, and said: they are all the same.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim

cards.x: Al-Quduri: riba is in anything measured by volume or weight, when sold for the same kind with an increase. Like for like is allowed; with an increase it is not.
cards.src: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, Chapter on Riba

cards.x: Al-Ghazali lists riba among the common wrongs of the marketplace that must be stopped.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good

checks.q: Who did the Prophet ﷺ curse in the hadith on riba?
checks.a: The one who takes it, pays it, writes it and witnesses it
w: Only the one who takes it
The one who takes it and the one who pays it
checks.why: All four were cursed, and he said they are all the same.

checks.q: Selling a kilo of dates for two kilos of dates, on the spot, is…
checks.why: Same kind, weighed or measured, with an increase is riba.

checks.q: Selling gold for the same weight of gold, hand to hand, is…
checks.why: Like for like of the same kind is allowed.

lessons.title: Honesty in trade
lessons.about: Cheating in the market, from al-Ghazali.

cards.x: Al-Ghazali names, among the common wrongs of the market, lying about what you paid for goods so you can sell at a 'profit'. Whoever knows of it should tell the buyer.
cards.src: Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, Book of Commanding Good: wrongs of the market

cards.x: Hiding a fault in what you sell is also forbidden. Whoever knows the fault must point it out, or he is content with his brother's loss.

title: Dealing with Doubts
sub: What to do with doubts, from the Prophet ﷺ and Imam al-Ghazali

lessons.title: A doubt is not disbelief
lessons.about: What the Prophet ﷺ said to Companions troubled by thoughts.

cards.x: Some Companions told the Prophet ﷺ they found thoughts in themselves too terrible to speak. He asked, 'Do you really find that?' They said yes. He said: 'That is clear faith.'
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

cards.x: The Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan comes and asks: who created this, who created that, until he asks who created your Lord. When that happens, seek refuge in Allah and stop.
cards.src: Hadith, al-Bukhari and Muslim

cards.x: Being troubled by such a thought shows your faith rejects it. You are not blamed for a passing thought.
cards.src: Hadith, Sahih Muslim, Book of Faith

checks.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ call hating these whispers?
checks.why: He said, 'That is clear faith', about the Companions who were troubled by them.

checks.q: When the thought 'who created Allah?' comes, you should…
checks.a: Seek refuge in Allah and stop
checks.why: The hadith's instruction is to seek refuge in Allah and stop.

checks.q: Is a person sinful for a passing doubt they dislike?
w: Only if it lasts a day
checks.why: Disliking it shows faith; a passing thought is not held against you.

lessons.title: Al-Ghazali's own doubts
lessons.about: A great Imam's honest account of his crisis.
